title: Requirements and output contracts
summary: A requirements contract measures quantity by the buyer’s needs; an output contract measures quantity by the seller’s production. The agreed arrangement and good-faith limits constrain those quantities.
notes:
These contracts allow parties to commit before they know an exact quantity. Structural Polymer explains why a buyer’s initially small or zero requirements do not necessarily make the promise illusory. It also examines exclusivity and a price-matching provision. UCC § 2-306 supplies relevant limits, including the treatment of stated estimates and disproportionate demands. A later claim that a party manipulated requirements is a claim about performance of an obligation and must be distinguished from the claim that no obligation ever existed.

Structural Polymer explains why variable or temporarily zero requirements need not make an agreement illusory. The source inquiry includes whether demand is genuine, the role of a price-matching clause, and the good-faith constraints associated with UCC § 2-306. The breadcrumb-output problem asks whether shutting production after losses is consistent with the bargain. The full assigned statutory text remains a separate source item where the excerpt only discusses it.
